findings.title: Queue.shutdown does not exist on Python <3.13, shutdown hangs
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). queue.Queue.shutdown was added in Python 3.13. On older runtimes this raises AttributeError, which is caught and logged per-queue, leaving workers blocked forever in work_queue.get(). Worker.join(timeout=5.0) then times out and close()/terminate() never actually stops workers. Consequence is leaked daemon threads and hung consumer shutdown/rebalance.

findings.title: Offsets marked complete even when processing fails
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block after result_processor. Any exception is logged and swallowed, then the offset is still marked done, so get_committable_offsets advances past failures. This contradicts the class docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and bypasses Arroyo DLQ handling, which requires the strategy to raise. Consequence is silent data loss: transient DB/cache errors cause uptime results to be skipped and committed as if successful.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit() does add_offset then non-blocking put. The docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' but there is no bound, so if Kafka polling outpaces workers the process enqueues unboundedly. Consequence is unbounded memory growth and OOM when a queue backs up, plus unbounded growth of OffsetTracker sets.

findings.title: Offsets committed from background thread
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy spawns a commit_thread that every second calls get_committable_offsets then commit_function, which in result_consumer.py calls Arroyo commit(). That Commit callback is owned by the StreamProcessor poll thread and tied to partition assignment. Calling it concurrently from a background thread races with rebalance/close/terminate, committing revoked partitions or committing while Arroyo is tearing down the strategy. Consequence is commit errors, lost commits, or duplicates.

findings.title: Factory-shared queue pool is shut down by per-assignment strategy
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and hands the same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned by create_with_partitions. But SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), and factory.shutdown() also shuts it down. After a rebalance the old strategy kills workers/queues still referenced by the factory, so the next strategy reuses a dead pool and stops processing, while multiple live strategies would share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit loops. Consequence is a stalled consumer after the first rebalance.

findings.title: close() loses final commits; terminate() leaks commit thread
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event then joins commit_thread before draining workers via queue_pool.shutdown(). Offsets completed while workers drain after the commit thread exited are never committed. terminate sets the event but never joins the commit thread at all, leaving a daemon thread that can keep calling commit_function after partitions are revoked. Consequence is duplicate reprocessing on restart and commit-after-revoke errors.

findings.title: Committable scan iterates full offset range
findings.body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets computes min/max of all_offsets then loops for offset in range(start, max_offset+1). With a sparse gap the loop cost is proportional to the numeric gap, not the number of tracked offsets. A single missing offset with a large max can cause millions of iterations every second per partition. It should iterate the sorted tracked set instead. Consequence is CPU spikes and stalled commit loop under gaps.

findings.title: FilteredPayload handled via AssertionError
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload starts with assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload straight to this decoder, so every filtered message raises AssertionError, logs 'Failed to decode' or 'Error submitting message to queue', then is marked complete via the exception path. Filtered messages should return None explicitly without assert/exception. Consequence is noisy exception logs for normal filtered traffic and exception-driven control flow.

findings.title: wait_until_empty and stats ignore in-flight work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.get_stats sums q.qsize() and wait_until_empty polls total_items==0. qsize only counts items still queued, not the item already removed by Queue.get() and being processed by a worker with its offset still outstanding. wait_until_empty therefore can return True while work is still in flight and offsets uncommitted. Consequence is premature test synchronization and any production use would incorrectly assume quiescence.

findings.title: Hash distribution test is flaky
findings.body: test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 keys group0..group19 with hash(key)%3 hit all 3 queues. Python string hash is salted per process, so hitting all buckets is probabilistic, not guaranteed. The test can fail on some hash seeds despite correct code. It should mock hashing or assert consistency only, not full coverage. Consequence is flaky CI.

findings.title: Queue-depth assertion races with workers
findings.body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items then immediately asserts get_stats total_items>0. Workers start in FixedQueuePool.__init__ and can drain the unbounded queues before the assertion runs, making total_items==0 and failing the test nondeterministically. The test needs to pause workers or poll until expected state instead of asserting transient queue depth. Consequence is flaky CI.
